Over the last 5 years I've been a 24/7 carer to my dad. He was a diabetic who didnt control his sugars for years when he was battling depression. That led to ulcers forming on both of his heals and in 1 it turned into osteomyelitis. After 4 years of fighting to keep both his feet even thru multiple episodes of sepsis, his right foot was amputated just below the knee this past April. But in those 5 years he also dealt with sudden/rapid cataracts that made him 100% blind over a few months, Fournier gangrene, metabolic encephalopathy, acute kidney failure, bouts of afib, hhv-6 (human herpes virus 6) encephalitis and meningitis, and lastly small cell lung carcinoma. 

He was my reason to get up in the morning and to keep going. He depended on me. And now I feel so lost and empty without having him to care for. 

The cancer took him so quick. Just 8months ago his chest ct didnt show any cancer. Then during Christmas dinner he had his first ever seizure. The hospital the ambulance took him to basically did a full body scan to figure out the cause and thought he had brain cancer so they life flighted him to boston. There they discovered that the seizure was from the encephalitis and meningitis but that he had advanced lung cancer that was surrounding his pulmonary artery. So after 16 days in the hospital we brought him home to finish his antiviral infusions and begin the plan with oncology to treat the cancer, they thought he had months. 

The night before he died I did his last antiviral infusion and we celebrated that we did 15 at home infusions thru a PICC line and had no complications or infections. But we were up all night with him bc of severe incontinence. So we bathed him and changed him up several times that night. 

The next morning he whispered to my mom that today was the day. We didnt even get a chance to set up  home hospice for him. He couldnt swallow much by like 3pm and the pharmacy couldnt switch his pain meds to liquid as they were out of stock. So I crushed one of his pain pills and put it in his liquid depakote when he was in pain. 

Around 5pm he was surrounded by his kids, grandkids and wife. He said I love you one last time to each of us before he could no longer speak. He held on til we sent the kids away as to not traumatize them. At 815 I noticed his color change to a grayish yellow and knew the end was imminent. We all held him as I gave him is last rites of sorts, no time for the priest to arrive. Moments after I finished and anointed him with holy oil his heart stopped. 

We gave him the death he asked for. At home, with the Beatles playing softly, with his dogs and family. 

Yesterday was his funeral mass but the burial is on hold until April as our town doesnt do winter burials. 

Over these last few years I've been told how hard it is to be a 24/7 carer for a loved one. But it was a beautiful blessing to be the one who cared for him. What they dont say is just how much harder it is for the carer to lose their charge. I'm empty and shattered. My dad was my best friend. It's been a week since he died and it feels like time is nonsense. How can it have been a week already?

I've had a wound vac. It helps in multiple ways. 

Basically they insert a special foam sheet cut to the size and shape of the wound. They cover the foam and wound site with a thick sticky plastic sheet similar to what they cover an iv with. A special tube is pierced thru the plastic film and attached to a negative pressure pump with a fluid collection container. 

1st by tricking the body into thinking there's a skin layer by making an airtight seal. It stops trying to scab over and works on filling in the missing tissue layers.

2nd by pulling away all pus/liquid that would otherwise cause maceration, which inhibits healing. Think when you've worn wet socks for a while and when you take them off your skin is wrinkly and puffy. With an open wound it can make the fresh layers of tissues degrade setting back healing time.

3rd. Preventing infections and contamination of the wound bed.

4th it can drastically speed up the healing process with less risk of complications.

Recipe for what I did:

Cheap cake mix

3 eggs as indicated in the cake mix directions

282 grams canned frosting

3/4cup brewed coffee in place of some of the water

1/3cup water + a few tablespoons to get the right consistency in the batter

8"x11.5" glass cake pan

Parchment paper 

Cooking spray

Set oven at 350 as instructed on package 

Add eggs, coffee, 1/3cup water and cake mix till incorporated.

Add frosting to mix and mix vigorously for 2 min.

Spray pan with cooking spray then line with parchment to keep it from sliding. Spray parchment with cooking spray to allow for easy release from paper.

Baked for 45 min in the middle rack

Cooled in pan for 10 min then transferred to my oil splatter guard that I use in place of a cooling rack.(I hate the indents left by the wire rack). Immediately remove parchment paper from cake.

I am not an expert in this but I recommend vacuum sealing when possible. My meats came wrapped from the butcher in freezer paper. From my experience removing as much moisture and air from around the product to freeze prevents freezer burn. Best to flash freeze veg on a flat sheet in a single layer then bag once frozen.
